label: Officer Manipulated an Object to Identify It (Not Plain Feel)
motion_heading: The Officer's Manipulation of an Object During the Pat-Down Exceeded the Plain-Feel Doctrine

excluded_explanations.display_note: You aren't sure yet what the officer did during the pat-down, so this issue wasn't drafted. If body-cam footage or the report shows the officer kept squeezing or manipulating an object after it was clearly not a weapon, that's the plain-feel problem.

rule_statements.text: An officer conducting a lawful frisk may seize an object without a warrant only if its incriminating character is immediately apparent from the lawful pat-down itself.

Once the officer has concluded that an object is not a weapon, continued squeezing, sliding, or manipulating of it to determine what it is exceeds the scope of a lawful frisk and is an unconstitutional search.
Evidence obtained through a search that exceeds the lawful scope of a frisk must be suppressed.

practice_notes: The officer's report often gives the game away — phrases like 'I manipulated the object' or 'I felt what I believed, based on training, to be narcotics' after ruling out a weapon are exactly the Dickerson fact pattern.
